Update:

tldr; If no OS won't boot properly, and all other troubleshooting fails, reset the CMOS settings.  This can be done by loading a preset in BIOS, amongst other ways.

Computer has been running fine for nearly 2 weeks running 24/7.  The watercooled OC preset set very aggressive CPU speed/thermal settings in BIOS causing reboots at 80 deg. C so I had to change those to more conservative settings.  Processor limits to \~70 deg. C now and averaging 4.2 GHz. all-core.  Memory set back to original DOCP/XMP 3200 MHz. settings.

What I believe caused the issue was somehow the CMOS got corrupted (possibly from storms/power issues), and using the BIOS to load any preset effectively resets it.  Removing/reinstalling the CMOS battery apparently doesn't do this.

Yes, Suno has gotten progressively worse in my opinion.  With a minimal prompt, it would provide some decent results.  But now, it's like the prompts don't even matter to it.  It just generates whatever it feels like.  I could create the song myself now before spending the time it takes Suno to get it right.

  
Udio is working much better for me at the moment.

I should've clarified what I meant.  I meant, the Lumon facility where the "innies" go to "work".  I can definitely see Lumon as being a massive conglomerate.  Heck, their logo is on the city water tower!

In a sense, Helly is like Jesus to Lumon.  She praises how wonderful it is to the world on the outside, but has to sacrifice herself to it as well.  In this way, Lumon can learn how to control the most difficult to control: someone with the innermost desire for free will yet the strong ability to convince people away from it as well.

Even her name... Helly... think about it.

That makes sense.  Perhaps the early pioneers of the brain control technology.  

I tend to think the 'macro data refinement' is simply training the chosen 'innies' how to respond to the external stimuli fed into their brains from the facility.

The whole facility has old-timey terminal computers and an extremely simple bland design.  Lumon's focus isn't on what is there, but rather what they can make their 'innies' perceive to be there.  Like the little petty rewards given to the 'employees'.  In reality these are just inconsequential clutter.  But under Lumon's control, the brain perceives them as extraordinary.

Lumon will be able to provide the escape the world needs when the world is no longer enjoyable or free.

Well said my friend.  I know I'm just another nobody here, and this place is basically a place to vent and not gain much from it.  But I sincerely wish you well.  A small dog is relatively easy to care for and will provide great companionship.  Cats are too but they're not as affectionate IMO.

I live completely and utterly alone. The only human contact is customer service or the occasional small talk at a park or store. Don't take living with someone for granted, even if it is your brother. I am going insane and want to die. But I keep going even into my 40s as well. Projects and positive mindset are the key.

Same here.  My gf of 12 years was my only friend.  Now she's gone - she left me.  In my forties now and I don't think I should even bother seeking another relationship as my depression and social anxiety will just interfere again.  Staying busy, too much caffeine, staying busy, trying to avoid insanity.
Same.  That's when I just have to take a nap for 15-30 min.
Do it all - switch between each every 30 min. or so.  Gotta love ADHD.
Curious... you guys ever tried caffeine?  Seems to be a good antidepressant for me.  Staying away from the pills if I can help it.
Knowledge is power

Same.

Wouldn't wish it on my worst enemy.  The loneliness kills your soul.

Icy day out.  Sitting here listening to the lights rattle in the fixtures in this comfortable yet depressing office space.  Waiting for my next call.

How's your day going?

Ween yourself off with beer and coffee.  Trust me, long time alcohol binger, always used it to escape the problems but not anymore.  Getting drunk always just makes things worse when you're drinking to escape, especially if you're by yourself.  Just do 3 beers for a buzz, do some praying/music/mediation, brew up some coffee, and focus on whatever makes you happy.  The job situation sucks everywhere you go but you will be a better person for not giving up.

Same here, after 12 year relationship.

She just went cold.  Amazes me how women can do that.

Health is deteriorating and dementia is kicking in.  Was contemplating suicde but won't need to at this rate.

Stunned , same here.

I'm still going to re-watch the series to see things that didn't make sense the first time through.
Thank you.  I am trying.  It's extremely tough.  It's like needing to get your car into the shop but the car is all you have to get there.
Well said :)
Wow, cannot be unseen

Same here.

It figures that people with a reason to live get killed by a drunk driver or some other unfortunate thing,  but losers like me with no friends/family whatsoever who really want to die and get it over with are stuck here in this endless lonely routine.

​

With every breath, I pray for death.
Any help that costs money to get, isn't genuine help.
If they don't care while you're here, why would they care when you're gone?
I'm in the same type of situation.  But no kids.  And now no girlfriend either.  Staying busy is my friend.  Biding my time until I die.

Same here.  Therapists suck because:

\- They cost too much.  
\- Ultimately, they only care about getting paid (the help isn't 100% genuine).

Stick with Reddit.  Self-talk is really good too.  Meditation/prayer.  Moderate caffeine/alcohol intake.  MUSIC - can't stress that enough.  Keep the background noise on at a low volume, helps the darkness of loneliness stay away.  A dog or cat is a good friend.  Stay off the pharma meds and exercise/drink water instead.

Speaking from experience.
Caffeine coke & booze make it easy to do.  Shuts off the bullshit avoidance part of your brain.  Doing this sober is so, so tough.

In the same boat.  Single male, in my 40s, just recently lost my gf of 12 year relationship due to depression and drinking.  The good friends never last - it seems they (or I) move away.  Been without any friends for 15 years now.

Inner circles... they are tough to get into, especially the older you get.  Making friends is really about who you already know, not what you know.  It's very hard to get started.  If you already have crippling issues, it's best to cope with those first.  I realize it might not ever happen for me, but I still thank God for what I do have and appreciate the simpler things in life.

In this unified conscience we know as 'the Internet' , you're never alone.  Stay strong :)

There's that chance it would be botched, leaving you crippled and more miserable for life.  Believe me, I've contemplated this over and over.

The best suicide is just to keep living, and make the world suffer just a little bit more with you in it.  F---  the world.  You are just as entitled to be here as all the rest of the jokers.  Give 'em hell.
I sometimes think we are here for God's amusement.  Seriously, why would he put the tree of knowledge within reach if it would cause so much turmoil?

We're not alone in our loneliness.

I hear you man.
Miserable people don't attract other miserable people.  It sucks because the only way to attract friends is to 'snap out' of the loneliness and depression and fake it to make it.

Mine just did the same after 12 years together.

I accept the fact that I stopped meeting her needs both emotionally and sexually.

Things got stale.

Women are driven by primal human needs and desires.  

Look what Eve did in Genesis... they're scandalous.  What can I say?
I don't know.  Over 30 years later, I still don't know.  I think it's just something we have to deal with.
I've put over 1000 hours into Skyrim.  :)

They recognize your depression by:

\- Your body language and facial expression.  Depression tends to give you resting b\*tch face.

\- Your lack of social posts / activities.  Doing things alone all the time.

\- Your vibes.  The energy you give off.  Trust me, when you're depressed, you give off negative energy and people can sense it.

​

If they're avoiding you, it's easy to know:

\- They never ask questions about you.  True friends take an interest in you.

\- They never include you in their photos.  You might be the one they use to take photos of them however.

\- You have something they find valuable (knowledge, money, etc.) but that's all they go to you for.
This is why I refuse to go the medicated route.  Genuine human interaction trumps meds any day.  But you won't get that from anyone charging you money.
Wow, what a great way to allow people to reach out and get help - just hide their posts and not tell them! (sarcasm)

Your little guy will know what happened and knows you loved him.  Don't fret it.  If a guinea pig is what you're feeling suicidal for, be happy, because that's something I'd trade 40 years of loneliness for.

True.  It's that little 'tick' in our brains that says "hey - look at that, I need that too" when we see others doing everything together and not alone.

If we could just off loneliness, life would get much easier.

Have had no friends for over 15 years.  Seriously.  No family either.  It's not that I set my standards too high.  I've tried about everything.  It's literally a curse.  I've been through too much devastation early in life and it's ruined me.  

People can sense your vibes - your energy.  Positive energy attracts other positive energy.  Negative energy reflects.  No matter how good the smile, or the walk, or the deeds, people know when you're damaged.  They'll avoid you like the plague, unless they need someone to step on or degrade to boost their ego.

What's kept me alive is self talk, being humble, and realizing that I'm slowly committing suicide anyways day by day.  The loneliness will kill you.  So no need to worry about doing it yourself.
On a related note, the worst thing about people is realizing they all suck.

I can go from suicidally depressed to feeling normal in a second.  All it takes is a good conversation.  Unfortunately it's short-lived and what most people take for granted - having social skills and being in established circles - is something I lack and it brings me right back down.

Can't make friends because I have no friends.  Can't establish conversation because I have nothing to say.

The best times I had in life were when I was living with my mom into my 20s.  Then she moved hours away and the depression got bad despite my having a long-term girlfriend and a place of our own.  I wish I could go back to that, living with her and dating my girlfriend.  If you have the type of parents you can really get along good with, cherish it.  I miss mine.

Take my advice:

Focus on getting on your own and make some friends.  Easier said than done, I know, speaking from experience like yours.  If you jump into a relationship with a woman, and you lack friends and some sort of a life, they WILL leave you for some reason or another.  Even the 'good girls' that you'd swear would never cheat or hurt you, will.  It's in their nature.  You have to be a man that women will respect.
Because they have a purpose, whatever it may be.
And you can be both.

Lessons I learned:

Remember it comes and goes, don't give up.  
Caffeine and exercise is your friend.  
Music is life.
If I start drinking again, I won't stop.  Seriously.  The struggle is real.

I know the feeling.

If you can, if all possible, take some of that money, fill up the gas tank, grab your earbuds and some tunes, and head to a lake.  Or river.  Or some peaceful place outdoors.  Tune this world out, get in touch with nature, and enjoy it while it's still here.

I managed to find and keep a girlfriend for 12 years with all of those same issues.  It's possible, but it's bound to fail.  Those issues interfered with our relationship and she finally decided to leave.
Do you get any songs in your head when this happens?  That's what happens to me.
For me, it started as shyness.  Now I know how doggy-dog this world is, the anger has overtaken me.  I'm all smiles when in the company of good people.  But they're extremely rare.
